title: Packaging progress: 3 recent sustainability wins - The Campbell's Company
summary: Campbell's is committed to advancing packaging sustainability and believe meaningful progress comes from continuously innovating and improving the way we design, source and package our products.
body_markdown:
We are committed to advancing packaging sustainability and believe meaningful progress comes from continuously innovating and improving the way we design, source and package our products.


Check out these 3 recent packaging upgrades we’re proud to have completed:


**1. Rao’s Homemade® 2-packs now use paper sleeves.**


- **What we did:** Our 31.7 oz. 2-pack *Rao’s* *Homemade* jars used plastic dog bone packaging that was not recyclable. We swapped this to a paper-based Cluster-Clip™.
- **Why it matters:** This packaging not only offers more ergonomic handling and easier removal but is also fully recyclable.
- **What’s next:** *Rao’s* *Homemade* plans to transition all remaining formats to this type of packaging by the first quarter of fiscal 2027.


**2. We redesigned Prego *®* jars for improved recyclability.**


- **What we did:** We removed mixed-material layers that prevented recycling from 38oz. and 45oz. *Prego* plastic Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles in October 2024. We also redesigned 4 million jar openings and steel closures.
- **Why it matters:** Removing mixed-material layers made over 31 million bottles recyclable in 2025. In just five months, the redesigned *Prego* jar has saved 62,000 and 7,000 pounds of glass and metal.


**3. We increased recycled material used in our *Snyder’s of Hanover* pretzel canisters.**


- **What we did:** We added 25% post-consumer recycled (PCR) content to PET pretzel canisters.
- **Why it matters:** This change adds recycled material content to the canister while maintaining current product protection standards consumers expect in this format.


While we are proud of this progress, we know there is still more work to do. We will continue to invest in packaging innovations that help improve recyclability and reduce environmental impact.

## FAQs


## How does Campbell’s support recycling and/or biodegradable materials?


Like you, we know that the small choices we make, such as the packaging we use, can make


a big difference


over time. Across our brands, we are working to make our packaging more sustainable. For example, we removed mixed-material layers that prevented recycling from


38oz


and


45oz


Prego PET bottles in October 2024, making over 31 million bottles recyclable in 2025. We also redesigned Prego jar openings across 4 million jars and steel closures, saving 62K and 7K pounds of glass and metal, respectively, since May 2025. In addition, as part of our commitment to transparency, Campbell’s continues to use


[How2Recycle](https://how2recycle.info/) labeling to help consumers make informed decisions about how to responsibly dispose of our packaging.


## How does Campbell’s approach sustainable packaging?


Packaging serves essential functions by protecting product quality, ensuring food safety, reducing food waste, and providing consumers with information they need in a convenient format. Campbell’s is committed to advancing packaging sustainability while


maintaining


these critical functions


, recognizing


that meaningful progress requires both internal innovation and industry-wide collaboration.


By


2025, we


ha


d


transitioned


95%


of our packaging to recyclable or industrially compostable designs and materials, towards our goal of 100% by 2030.


## How does Campbell’s consider environmental impact when designing packaging?


Campbell’s


continues to invest in packaging innovations that improve recyclability and reduce environmental impact. We are working to


reduce weight and material use, integrate more post-consumer recycled content, and shift


components to more recyclable materials


across our


portfolio


.


## Does the packaging of your food contain BPA?


We use non-BPA lining in all


our aluminum and steel cans throughout our operations in North America.


PET bottles,


pouches


and


cartons


– such

V8

Swanson


broths


and


Campbell’s

(and have always been) non-BPA packaging.


The containers of a few other products have metal components with limited food contact


points


,


but


are key to ensuring lids


remain


tight. BPA is used as a coating on that metal but in


small amounts


.


Although


the FDA has


determined

people would prefer to avoid
